analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md and the supplied change map/patch. The new addon command documentation (HEAD changed range 904–932; partially visible patch) introduces inspection, placement and release of VM-related holds through an asserted owner-only lifecycle mailbox bound to the live process. No implementation or complete command contract is supplied here, so the asserted authorization and process binding are unverified, not observed missing controls. No concrete regression is supported by this documentation-only evidence.
Reviewed surrounding lifecycle draining/restart behavior (BASE 904–963), residency and private diagnostics (982–1023), cache failure/precision posture (1052–1159), benchmark integrity and qualification limits (1306–1419), update verification, fan authority, logout/enrollment, refusal logging and bounded evidence uploads (1437–1701). Relevant contracts include A-001, A-008, A-016, TB-003, TB-007, TB-010, TB-011, T-010, T-041, T-043, T-047, T-053 and T-058; these surrounding sections are unchanged according to the complete range map and are not new findings.
Integration should inspect AddonCommand.swift and its mailbox/hold handlers: enforce owner authorization and live-process binding on status/hold/release, bound and expire holds, and reconcile hold effects with memory eviction, idle unloading, graceful drain/restart and serving authorization. Check whether hold status exposes request-derived data and whether VM resource contention creates a new availability assumption requiring threat-model coverage. The incomplete patch and absence of executable changes prevent resolving these material new-surface questions in this source pass.
